recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-7962 unless a future work group decision changes the external THO substance-category terminology.
issue_request: FHIR-7962 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification request to add a Substance class property. The final resolution asked for a Substance category element with cardinality 0..*, type CodeableConcept, and an extensible value set covering allergen, biological, body, chemical, dietary, drug/medicament, and material categories.
initial_application: Git commit 7e22e5f2f59444e875ad6a9fcf3e425a8e280064 explicitly says "#7962 add.category to substance" and added Substance.category, examples, a category search parameter, and valueset-substance-category.xml. Later source rework commits, including 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 and c69d71aa213de86d55e0261339c15e4bacd509e6, preserved the element in the current StructureDefinition source form.
additional_context: Substance is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/substance/structuredefinition-Substance.xml is in current build scope. The current Substance.category differential remains tagged #7962, has max *, type CodeableConcept, and an extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-category. The value set includes the THO substance-category code system, and the local THO package contains the requested concepts with definitions. No direct Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source edits were made because the current authoritative source already satisfies the applied Jira decision.
source_changes: No source changes; current build-scoped Substance source already has the requested category element, binding, value set reference, and search parameter.
